subject: Operator & Subprocessor Notice - DPA redlines and eSign coordination
messages:
From: Jacob Turner <jacob.turner@medicorp.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: MediCorp Legal <privacy@medicorp.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: DPA - operator/subprocessor notice questions (attached redlines)

Naomi,

Thanks for sending the draft. Attached are our first-pass redlines (MediCorp_DPA_Redlines_v1.docx). We have a few specific asks we want to confirm before we return an execution-ready copy:

1) Operator/Subprocessor notice window: your draft says "as soon as practicable" — can we get a defined notice period (30 days) for any new subprocessors or a carve-out for security patches?
2) EU->US transfer mechanism: we noted clause 7 references SCCs but also allows future mechanisms. Please confirm whether Redwood will sign an EU addendum or if you prefer an Annex approach.
3) Data localization: we have a small scope of customer data that (per regulation) must remain within the EU. Can you confirm any options to pin region for specific workloads under Dedicated/Private?
4) eSign path: do you support DocuSign (preferred) or only AdobeSign? We need the audit trail preserved.

CC'ing legal in case they want to propose alternate language. Happy to schedule a short call if helpful.

Best,
Jacob Turner
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
MediCorp Health

Attachments: MediCorp_DPA_Redlines_v1.docx (docx)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Turner <jacob.turner@medicorp.com>
Cc: MediCorp Legal <privacy@medicorp.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Apr 2028 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: DPA - operator/subprocessor notice questions (attached redlines)

Jacob —

Thanks for the detailed redline. Appreciate the clear asks. High level answers up front, below I flagged the items that will need counsel sign-off.

1) Subprocessor notice window: we typically do "as soon as reasonably practicable" with a 30-day notice for planned onboarding and an exceptions carve-out for emergency security patches. Counsel prefers the flexibility for security patches. If you require a strict 30-day rule for all changes, we can ask COO/legal, but it may impact our security response SLAs.

2) EU->US transfers: Redwood is prepared to execute the current EU SCCs as an addendum. We can also include wording to accept future transfer mechanisms once authorized by the EU Commission; we often include an annex that references the SCCs + migration language.

3) Data localization: for Dedicated and Private deployments we can offer regional pinning for the customer's workload. For Hosted API we cannot guarantee per-customer regionally restricted storage except for exports/backup retention configurations — I'll have Monica share the exact options.

4) eSign: we support both DocuSign and AdobeSign. DocuSign is fine — we can route this to DocuSign and preserve the audit trail.

Next steps I propose:
- Internal counsel will review the redlines and highlight any non-starters (I expect 2–3 clauses).
- I'll schedule a 30 min alignment call with you + our counsel and ops next week.
- If DocuSign is fine, we'll prepare an execution copy and link it in DocuSign for a single-signature route (Redwood then MediCorp).

Attaching a short summary of our counsel's initial notes (Redline_Summary_Naomi_v1.pdf) and our subprocessor inventory export for reference.

Would you be available Tue 10 Apr 10:00–10:30 ET?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Privacy Operations, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: Redline_Summary_Naomi_v1.pdf (pdf), Subprocessor_Inventory_2028-04-05.csv (csv)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Apr 2028 15:27:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: MediCorp DPA redlines - quick counsel Qs

Team —

Looping you on Jacob's redlines. Two items need legal posture and two need product/ops confirmation. Quick ask below — please reply inline: 

A) Subprocessor notice window — legal: do we accept 30-day planned notice + security patch carve-out? Monica: if we accept, what is the operational playbook for emergency onboarding and post-incident notification?

B) SCCs vs annex — legal: we prefer SCCs + migration language. Any reason to insist on an addendum rather than an annex?

C) Regional pinning — product/ops: can Dedicated workloads be pinned to EU region for both runtime and backups? If yes, what's the SLA differential / cost delta (ballpark)? Aditya, please provide a note I can share externally.

D) eSign routing — engineering: DocuSign link + audit trail is supported. Any retention caveats we should flag?

Thoughts: I think Jacob will accept the 30-day planned notice plus explicit carve-out for emergency patching; counsel will probably ask for language that allows us to onboard critical infra providers with notice "as soon as reasonably practicable" and to publish a monthly subprocessor log.

Please flag any absolute blockers. Planning to send an aligned reply to Jacob on Mon 9 Apr and propose Tue 10 for the call.

Thanks,
Naomi

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Turner <jacob.turner@medicorp.com>
Cc: MediCorp Legal <privacy@medicorp.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: DPA - operator/subprocessor notice questions (attached redlines)

Jacob —

Thanks again for the clear redlines and the questions. Per our internal review (summary attached), see our proposed compromise language below and next steps for execution via DocuSign.

1) Subprocessor notice: Proposed language — "Redwood will provide written notice of the engagement of any new Subprocessor at least thirty (30) days prior to such engagement, except in the case of emergency security patches or incident-response services, where Redwood may engage a Subprocessor on shorter notice and will notify Customer as soon as reasonably practicable following such engagement."
- We will also publish a monthly subprocessor inventory (static URL) for transparency.

2) Transfers: We will execute the EU SCCs as an addendum and include migration language that permits use of any future transfer mechanism approved by the EU Commission.

3) Regional pinning: For Dedicated and Private deployments we can pin workloads to the EU for both runtime and backups. For Hosted API the default is multi-region infrastructure; we can provide an on-request export/retention policy that limits storage location for customer-managed backups. Monica will share a short options matrix.

4) eSign & audit trail: DocuSign is acceptable. We'll send the final DPA via DocuSign (single sign flow: MediCorp -> Redwood). The envelope will include a PDF of the executed DPA and the DocuSign audit trail. Link below when live.

Attached is our counsel's summary of remaining negotiation points (Redline_Summary_Naomi_v1.pdf). Unless you mark anything as a hard stop, we will prepare an execution copy reflecting the above and route it via DocuSign this week.

DocuSign placeholder: https://docusign.example.com/placeholder/abc123-DC-1987
Drive folder with docs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cDPA-DC-1987

Proposed call: Tue 10 Apr 10:00–10:30 ET — can you confirm? If not, we can handle via redlines and exchange.

Best regards,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Privacy Operations, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: Redline_Summary_Naomi_v1.pdf (pdf)
